newsitem.title: USA: Simpson custody judge slams Brown family.
newsitem.headline: Simpson custody judge slams Brown family.

text.p: The judge who gave O.J. Simpson custody of his children said the family of his murdered ex-wife Nicole Brown were unfit guardians who tried to make the children hate their father, the New York Post reported on Wednesday.

In a sealed Jan. 31 ruling obtained by the newspaper, Orange County, California, Superior Court Judge Nancy Wieben Stock rejected a request from the Brown family to keep the children until an appeal against the custody ruling.

She said "residence in the Brown household was detrimental to the children ... these factors have included a highly emotionalized atmosphere of ill-feeling toward the father and unabated and unrestrained public expression of ill-feelings toward the father," the newspaper said.

"This atmosphere places the children at great emotional risk, both within the Brown household and ... outside, where the children are at risk of encountering friends and strangers who have been exposed to the expressed ill-feelings fostered by the grandparents," Stock wrote.

Former football star Simpson was cleared in criminal court in 1995 on charges of stabbing Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman to death in Los Angeles in June 1994, but he was held liable for the deaths in civil court this year.

Grandparents Lou and Juditha Brown had cared for the Simpsons' children Sydney, 11 and Justin, 8, after Simpson was charged in their daughter's murder. But Stock granted Simpson custody of the children.

The New York tabloid said Simpson had charged in court papers that racial slurs were used in the Brown home. The newspaper quoted family lawyer Nancy Roit as calling the claim "preposterous" and denying that ill-feeling had been created toward Simpson in the home.
